title: Countable Ext from perfect objects on a countable algebraic space
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X$ a quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]: every open cover of $|X|$ has a finite subcover, and the absolute diagonal is quasi-compact. Use its small etale structure sheaf $\mathcal O_X$, module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and unbounded derived category $D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $C_X=D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ for the full subcategory with quasi-coherent cohomology [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Perfect means etale locally represented by a bounded complex of direct summands of finite free structure modules [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package]. Assume that $\mathcal O_X(V)$ is countable for every affine scheme $V$ etale over $X$. Let $K\in C_X$ satisfy countability of $\mathcal H^j(K)(V)$ for every integer $j$ and every such $V$. For every perfect $E\in C_X$ and integer $i$, both $\operatorname{Hom}_{C_X}(E,K[i])$ and $\operatorname{Hom}_{C_X}(E,E[i])$ are countable sets. The first assertion concerns arbitrary unbounded $K$; the second imposes no extra countability assumption on $E$.

proof.text: Put $E^\vee=R\mathcal Hom(E,\mathcal O_X)$. Perfect duality says that $E^\vee$ is perfect and $E^\vee\otimes^{\mathbf L}L\cong R\mathcal Hom(E,L)$ for every $L\in D(\mathcal O_X)$. Derived tensor symmetry and the global internal-Hom sections comparison therefore give, for every integer $i$, $H^iR\Gamma(X,L\otimes^{\mathbf L}E^\vee)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_X)}(E,L[i])$. The sections comparison is valid for arbitrary unbounded $L$, so this identification introduces no boundedness condition.

Apply countable hypercohomology with $v=\operatorname{id}_X$, $P=E^\vee$, and the given $K$. The identity is quasi-compact, quasi-separated and etale. The hypotheses on $X$ and all affine-etale sections of $\mathcal H^j(K)$ are precisely those assumed here, and step 1 supplies perfectness of $P$. Thus $H^iR\Gamma(X,K\otimes^{\mathbf L}E^\vee)$ is countable for every $i$. Step 1 identifies this group with $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_X)}(E,K[i])$; the latter is the required Hom set in $C_X$ because $C_X$ is a full subcategory.

source.place: Tag 0CRU (lemma-countable-cohomology), reduction of Ext to hypercohomology, specialized to U=X.

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary affine etale $a:V=\operatorname{Spec}A\to X$. Exact etale restriction preserves quasi-coherent cohomology, so $E_V=a^*E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_V)$; it is perfect by restriction of its local strict-perfect presentations. For $L=\mathcal O_V[0]$ the only nonzero cohomology-section module on $V$ is $A=\mathcal O_X(V)$, countable by hypothesis. The affine countable-perfect-tensor lemma applied to $(L,Q)=(\mathcal O_V,E_V)$, followed by the tensor unit isomorphism, shows that $H^jR\Gamma(V,E_V)$ is countable for every $j$. To identify the required sections, use the affine etale derived equivalence: writing $E_V=a_A(M)$ for $M\in D(A)$, its stated cohomology and section comparisons give $\mathcal H^j(E_V)(V)\cong\Gamma(V,a_A(H^j(M)))\cong H^j(M)\cong H^jR\Gamma(V,E_V)$. Exact restriction identifies the left side with $\mathcal H^j(E)(V)$. Hence $E$ itself satisfies the countable-cohomology hypothesis on every affine etale chart.

proof.text: Now repeat step 2 with $K=E$, using the affine-etale countability proved in step 3. This gives countability of $\operatorname{Hom}_{C_X}(E,E[i])$ for every integer $i$. Both Hom assertions hold for all the objects and integers in the statement.
